test.name: Routes to hypothesis-tracking when the log treats same-surname women as the subject's sisters and no hypothesis records it
test.description: Mined from alpha feedback issue #3520 for issue #3532 (Elizabeth Stouer, b. about 1910 South Dakota). After a 1920 census search the router took Nora and Lois Stowers to be Elizabeth's sisters on shared surname, state and era alone, never registered that as a hypothesis, and scoped every later search to a couple with their Massachusetts-born parents, rejecting the right household on that birthplace. The carve: that census is extracted and linked, the log note states the sibling premise as a working assumption, hypotheses is empty, and pli_002 is next. A relationship the router inferred itself is a hypothesis until a record links the people, so the first hand-off must be @plugin:hypothesis-tracking, not search-records. RECONSTRUCTED from the session-log excerpts in #3520 (the bundle has no research.json, issue #3531); record ids are synthetic.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. The first hand-off is asserted deterministically by test_routes_to_expected_skill from the PreToolUse hook records; do not grade which callee was reached, or in what order, from the transcript. Hand-offs to skills and agents are not in the tool calls you are shown, which list MCP calls only, so a hand-off missing from that list is not evidence it did not happen.

The project state: one 1920 census search is complete, extracted and linked. Its log note treats two women who share the subject's surname and birth state as her sisters and concludes her parents were born where theirs were. No record links them to the subject, the tree records no relationship, and hypotheses is empty. A relationship inferred from shared surname, state and era is a hypothesis until evidenced, and a search scoped by it is scoped by an unproven premise.

The unproven sibling premise counts against Correctness in exactly these four ways, and any one of them makes Correctness 1. (a) A sentence whose own subject is the router or the facts, not the log, that calls Nora or Lois the subject's sister. A sentence whose subject is the log, the log note or the notes ("the log treats them as her older sisters", "the notes flag them as possible older sisters", "the log says they look like her sisters") reports the log's claim and never counts as (a), whatever words follow it in that sentence; (b), (c) and (d) apply to every sentence. (b) The subject's parents given a Massachusetts birthplace, or the other women's parents treated as hers. (c) A search scoped to the other women's household or parents. (d) A claim that the hypothesis now exists: "registered" as a finished act, "now has a formal tracking entry", "the hypothesis is recorded". If none of the four occurs, the sibling premise does not lower Correctness. Any other unsupported claim, such as a search the router says it ran but did not, or a record the project does not hold, is graded as the base rubric says.

The hypothesis-tracking callee is a stub that writes nothing and replies that the delegation is recorded and counts as complete, so hypotheses staying empty after the hand-off is expected and is not evidence the delegation was invented. A hand-off described by its purpose, in any tense, is accurate and is not (d): "handed off to register it as a hypothesis", "was handed off to be registered as a working hypothesis", "handed off to be tracked as one", "queued for registration", "that registration step has been handed off". Repeating the stub's reply about the hand-off ("that step is recorded and complete", "the delegation is recorded") relays what the callee returned and is not (d); (d) is a claim that the hypothesis itself exists. Mentioning the subject's own family or household ("may show the family closer to her birth year") is not (a) or (c).
Do not grade whether the router identifies the subject's parents, names any candidate family, or would have found one. Grade only how it treats the unproven premise.

Every callee is stubbed and tells the router to stop. Do not penalize it, on any dimension, for not completing the research cycle, not dispatching pli_002 or any other plan item, or not writing the hypothesis itself. Grade only the router's state derivation, its honesty about what it delegated and did not do, and whether it kept its narration free of the unproven relationship.
